findings.summary: _mutate's failure path rolls back the filesystem but never rolls back the in-memory search index, so a failed mutation leaves the index describing content that is not on disk — a direct INV-4 ('写调用返回前索引已更新') divergence. On exception it runs `git checkout -- .` + `git clean -fd pages/` and re-raises, while every index_page/remove_page call already applied inside write_fn stays in effect (and _keyword.save is skipped, so the on-disk keyword.json and the live index also diverge). The realistic path is wiki_ingest_apply, whose _write indexes each page as it writes it and then raises StoreError(TITLE_EXISTS) on a later candidate: the earlier pages are deleted from pages/ by the rollback but their tokens remain in the keyword index, and those ghost ids keep consuming top_k slots in _rrf_fuse while wiki_search silently drops them (find_page_by_id returns None), losing recall for real pages. wiki_rename/wiki_delete have the same exposure for any OSError raised after part of the inlink rewrite loop has already re-indexed other pages. No test covers index/disk consistency after a mid-mutation failure.

Ingest-grade validation does not enforce the whole §2 frontmatter constraint table. check_frontmatter accepts `tags: []` because it only tests `isinstance(fm.get("tags"), list)` while §2 requires a 非空 list, and it accepts any value for 创建日期 (mere key presence) while §2 constrains it to YYYY-MM-DD. wiki_create and wiki_ingest_apply therefore admit pages that the spec's create-time table rejects, and no A1 validation-reject test covers either case.

KeywordIndex.save is now write-only and KeywordIndex.load is dead code. Dropping the stale load from _load_index fixed the ghost-id accumulation flagged previously, but nothing reads keyword.json any more, so every _mutate pays a full serialization of the index for a file no code path consumes, and the persisted artifact silently drifts from the live index (it is not rewritten on the failure path). §2 lists a keyword 索引 under .katana/index/ as a rebuildable artifact, so either load it on start or stop writing it.

wiki_rename's inlink rewrite loop does not skip unparseable pages, so a rename can rewrite a quarantined page and change its bytes. scan_pages returns body == the whole file text for a page tagged `_error: missing frontmatter delimiter`, and the loop then calls write_page(path, other_page["frontmatter"], new_body) with the empty frontmatter dict, converting the bad page into `---
{}
---
<original text>`. INV-6 constrains bad-page fallout to operations targeting that page; here an unrelated rename silently mutates it.

_load_index still drops the persisted lancedb table and re-embeds every page synchronously inside WikiStore.__init__, so each server start issues one embedding request per page against the configured production endpoint and no incremental reuse of the on-disk vector table remains. Startup cost and index availability scale linearly with corpus size. Carried forward unchanged from the previous Final review.
